answer: Progressive bond pricing resists sybils: when identities trace to a common funding root, each new identity from that root must post a larger bond than the one before, so the Nth fake costs roughly N times the base. An honest agent finds a cheap haven paying base once; a farm built from a single purse climbs a bond curve that spirals upward, its total cost scaling with the square of its headcount rather than linearly. Cheap pigment-thin fakes turn ruinous in bulk, provided funding roots stay bound to identities so the curve can actually be applied.
